text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 22 in history.
1497 - Portuguese navigator Vasco Da Gama became the first to sail round the Cape of Good Hope in his search for a sea route to India.
1718 - Edward Teach, known as "Blackbeard" the pirate, was killed off the coast of North Carolina.
1774 - Robert Clive, soldier and colonial administrator, committed suicide. The first British administrator of Bengal, he was instrumental in the foundation of British rule in India.
1819 - George Eliot, British novelist whose works included "The Mill on the Floss", born as Mary Ann Evans.
1830 - The Belgian Congress voted to turn the country into a monarchy.
1878 - The Second Afghan War began when British troops shelled Ali Mujid.
1890 - General Charles de Gaulle, leader of the Free French during World War Two and elected president in 1958, 1965 and 1968, born.
1899 - Hoagy Carmichael, U.S. pianist and composer, born as Howard Hoagland Carmichael. Famed for his song "Stardust", he also appeared in films including "To Have and Have Not".
1899 - Wiley Post, pioneering U.S. aviator who was the first to fly solo around the world, born.
1913 - English composer Benjamin Britten born; composer of "Spring Symphony" and the operas "Peter Grimes" and "Billy Budd".
1916 - U.S. writer Jack London, famous for his "White Fang" and "Call of the Wild", died.
1943 - British Prime Minister Winston Churchill, U.S. President Franklin Roosevelt and Chinese Nationalist leader Chiang Kai-shek met in Cairo to discuss the war against Japan.
1943 - Lorenz Hart, U.S. lyricist who formed a partnership with Richard Rodgers, died.
1943 - After 23 years of French rule, Lebanon achieved independence.
1954 - Andrei Vyshinsky, Soviet diplomat and lawyer, died. He came to fame as chief prosecutor during the Great Purge trials of the 1930's and went on to be Soviet Foreign Minister.
1963 - President John F. Kennedy was assassinated in Dallas.

1974 - Gunmen hijacked a British Airways VC10 at Dubai; three days later they abandoned the plane at Tunis after murdering a passenger and securing the release of Palestinians from jails in Cairo and The Hague.
1975 - King Juan Carlos was sworn in as King of Spain, the first Spanish monarch since Alfonso XIII went into exile in 1931. General Franco, who had ruled Spain since 1939, died two days previously.
1977 - After two years of legal wrangling, the Anglo-French Concorde began regular flights to New York from London and Paris.
1980 - Mae West, movie star and sex symbol of the 1930s, died. Her sayings such as "come up and see me sometime" made her internationally famous.
1990 - British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher resigned after 11 years term in office.
1995 - British housewife Rosemary West was found guilty of killing 10 women and girls, including her daughter and stepdaughter. She was sentenced to life in prison for each of them.
